allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; white umbels.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its compound umbel drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind from the carrot family's inflorescence and its rays from its own, by the rules at the flowering plants; about 12 small white flowers about 2 mm across in each umbellet, by eye (no flora gives a count; the Flora of New Zealand gives the flower's size), the umbel 5 to 7 cm across. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on the inferior ovary, five stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Apiaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The leaf drawn twice pinnate (spec rework P4), its pinnae and their leaflets counted, set and shaped from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants and the plants; before, nine leaflets stood along one rachis. By eye: pinnae and leaflets 55 degrees from their rachises.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.leaflet_wid.note: A compound leaf's shape word describes its leaflets, so a leaflet's width follows the same chart as a blade's. Each word's width over length lies inside the band the Systematics Association's chart of plane shapes gives it, the value in the band the model's choice: lanceolate and oblanceolate 3:1 to 6:1 (0.25); elliptic, ovate and obovate 3:2 to 2:1 (0.57, 0.6, 0.6); orbicular about 1:1 (0.95); linear longer than 6:1, its sides parallel (0.08). The chart gives oblong and spatulate by their sides, not a band: 0.4 and 0.35 are the model's. A flora's two words ("ovate to lanceolate") read as the forms between them, so the width is their middle.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.leaflets.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.outline.note: Outlines drawn to the Systematics Association chart's definitions: lanceolate and ovate widest below the middle, oblanceolate and obovate above it, elliptic and orbicular at it, linear and oblong with their sides parallel, spatulate a broad rounded tip on a long narrow base. The curves are the model's, each the half-width as a share of the widest at 15 places from the base (u 0) to the tip (1), the same places for every word, so two words that tie draw the outline halfway between theirs. An ellipse for elliptic and orbicular, a rounded rectangle (a superellipse of power 4) for oblong. A compound leaf's word is its leaflets' (spec rework P4).

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a sprawling herb of soft, weak stems with parsley-like leaves and small umbels of white flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

generator.spreads.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
